title: Motion Graphs
learning_goal: Interpret position-time, velocity-time, and acceleration-time graphs and connect each graph to an object's motion.

stages.title: 1. Understand the idea
stages.content: Motion describes how an object's position changes over time. On a position-time graph, time is on the horizontal axis and position is on the vertical axis. The slope tells how quickly position changes.

stages.title: 2. Read a position-time graph
stages.content: A horizontal line means the object is at rest. A straight line sloping upward means constant positive velocity. A straight line sloping downward means constant negative velocity. A steeper line means a greater speed.

stages.title: 3. Worked example
stages.content: A student moves from 0 m to 12 m in 4 s. Change in position = 12 m. Change in time = 4 s. Average velocity = Δx/Δt = 12/4 = 3 m/s.

stages.title: 4. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A car moves from 5 m to 25 m in 5 s. What is its average velocity?
stages.hint: Start by finding the change in position: 25 − 5.
stages.alternate_explanation: Think of velocity as the slope of a position-time graph: rise over run, or change in position divided by change in time.

stages.title: 5. Velocity-time graphs
stages.content: The slope of a velocity-time graph represents acceleration. A horizontal line means constant velocity. An upward slope means positive acceleration. A downward slope means velocity is decreasing.

stages.title: 6. Acceleration-time graphs
stages.content: A horizontal line above zero means constant positive acceleration. A horizontal line below zero means constant negative acceleration. A line at zero means no acceleration, even though the object may still be moving.

stages.title: 7. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, explain motion from all three graph types, calculate velocity from position-time slope, calculate acceleration from velocity change, and match a motion description to the correct graph.

concept_cards.title: Read the axes before interpreting the line
concept_cards.content: A motion graph shows a measured quantity against time. It is not a picture of the road or path. Identify the vertical quantity and its unit first: the same line shape means different things on different graphs.

visual.label: Position increases uniformly: the slope represents velocity.

concept_cards.title: Position-time slope tells velocity
concept_cards.content: Average velocity is change in position divided by elapsed time. A rising straight line means constant positive velocity; a falling line means constant negative velocity. A horizontal segment means position does not change, so the object is at rest. A position below zero describes location, not necessarily direction.

visual.label: A falling position-time line: velocity is negative.

concept_cards.title: Velocity-time slope tells acceleration
concept_cards.content: Acceleration is change in velocity divided by elapsed time. A horizontal velocity line means zero acceleration, even when velocity is nonzero. Negative acceleration does not always mean slowing down: speed increases when velocity and acceleration have the same sign.

visual.label: Velocity decreases through zero, then becomes negative.

concept_cards.title: Signed area tells a change
concept_cards.content: Area under a velocity-time graph gives displacement; add signed areas above and below zero. Total distance uses the magnitudes of those areas. Area under an acceleration-time graph gives change in velocity, not velocity itself. You need an initial velocity to find final velocity.

visual.label: Rectangle: (3 m/s)(4 s) = 12 m displacement.

concept_cards.title: Acceleration-time height is acceleration
concept_cards.content: A constant line at +2 m/s² means velocity increases by 2 m/s each second. A line at zero means velocity stays constant; it does not by itself tell whether the object is stationary.

visual.label: Constant acceleration: velocity changes by +8 m/s in 4 s.

worked_examples.prompt: A position-time line connects (0 s, 2 m) and (4 s, 14 m). Find its velocity.

visual.label: A position-time line connects (0 s, 2 m) and (4 s, 14 m). Find its velocity.

solution_steps.explanation: Read final and initial positions from the vertical axis.
Use elapsed time, not just any time coordinate.
Positive slope means motion toward increasing position; a straight line means constant velocity.

worked_examples.prompt: A straight velocity-time line falls from +8 m/s at 0 s to 0 m/s at 4 s. Find acceleration.

visual.label: A straight velocity-time line falls from +8 m/s at 0 s to 0 m/s at 4 s. Find acceleration.

solution_steps.explanation: The velocity decreases, so its change is negative.
Slope, not graph height, gives acceleration.

solution_steps.equation: Velocity is positive while acceleration is negative.
solution_steps.explanation: Here the object slows down and reaches rest at 4 s. Negative acceleration would speed up an object already moving negatively.

worked_examples.prompt: A velocity-time graph is horizontal at +3 m/s from 0 to 4 s. Find displacement.

visual.label: A velocity-time graph is horizontal at +3 m/s from 0 to 4 s. Find displacement.

solution_steps.explanation: Displacement is signed area under the velocity-time graph.
The units reduce to meters and the area above zero is positive.
The horizontal slope means zero acceleration, although the object is moving.

worked_examples.prompt: Acceleration is +2 m/s² for 3 s. Find the change in velocity.

visual.label: Acceleration is +2 m/s² for 3 s. Find the change in velocity.

solution_steps.explanation: Area under acceleration-time gives change in velocity.
This is a change, not necessarily the final velocity.
An initial velocity is needed to calculate a final velocity.

guided_practice.prompt: A straight position-time line connects (0 s, 5 m) and (5 s, 25 m). Find velocity.

visual.label: A straight position-time line connects (0 s, 5 m) and (5 s, 25 m). Find velocity.

hint_steps: On this graph, velocity is the slope: vertical change divided by elapsed time.
Find vertical change: 25 − (5) = 20 m.
guided_practice.alternate_explanation: On this graph, velocity is the slope: vertical change divided by elapsed time.
alternate_explanation_steps: Find vertical change: 25 − (5) = 20 m.
Divide by 5 s: velocity = 4 m/s. The sign specifies the direction of the change.

conceptual_questions.prompt: A velocity-time graph is horizontal above zero. Explain whether the object is moving and whether it is accelerating.
expected_ideas: Velocity is positive and nonzero, so the object is moving in the positive direction.
Velocity is constant, so acceleration is zero.
misconceptions: A horizontal line always means the object is at rest.
conceptual_questions.follow_up: What quantity is on the vertical axis, and does it change with time?

visual.label: Constant positive velocity

conceptual_questions.prompt: A position-time graph is below zero but slopes upward. Explain the position and direction of motion.
expected_ideas: The object is on the negative side of the chosen origin.
Its position is increasing, so its velocity is positive.
misconceptions: Negative position necessarily means negative velocity.
conceptual_questions.follow_up: Is direction determined by the height of a position-time graph or its slope?

visual.label: Negative position with positive velocity

conceptual_questions.prompt: A velocity-time graph has equal areas above and below zero. Explain why displacement can be zero even though distance is not.
expected_ideas: Signed displacements in opposite directions cancel.
Distance adds the magnitudes of the traveled segments, so nonzero motion gives positive distance.
misconceptions: Zero displacement means the object never moved.
conceptual_questions.follow_up: What is the difference between adding signed changes and adding path lengths?

visual.label: Equal positive and negative velocity areas

conceptual_questions.prompt: An acceleration-time graph lies at zero. Can you conclude that the object is at rest? Explain.
expected_ideas: Zero acceleration means velocity is constant.
The constant velocity could be zero or nonzero; initial velocity is needed.
misconceptions: Zero acceleration always means zero velocity.
conceptual_questions.follow_up: Could an object maintain a nonzero velocity without changing it?

visual.label: Zero acceleration
